Code-to-text is tied at the source, 8/8, no inference. The Step 5b exemption is earned by the derivation pattern ('item IS the source column name'), not merely by mapping_basis, so no verify_<table>.R is owed. Value labels supplied the 1/5 anchors ('NOT AT ALL (1)' / 'EXTREMELY (5)'); the '(1)'/'(5)' code echoes were stripped and levels 2/3/4 left BLANK because the file labels them only with their own digit -- never padded with their own number. instructions are canonical PANAS present-moment wording (a level-3 source) because neither the .sav nor the PLOS article prints the administered instruction; the article reports only that participants rated adjectives 'to what extent they felt this way at that moment on a scale from 1 (not at all) to 5 (extremely)'. Canonical PANAS anchor boilerplate was deliberately NOT shipped because this study's anchors (not at all / extremely) differ from the PANAS original (very slightly or not at all / extremely). item_text and option_text are entirely study_materials. English administration, so no language/_translated columns. The pre anchors were checked against the source rather than copied from the post table and are IDENTICAL to it ('NOT AT ALL (1)'/'EXTREMELY (5)'), but the ITEM SET IS NOT: the pre measure is 8 adjectives, the post 12, and the article says so ('selecting eight items of the PANAS scale to assess positive affect (alpha = .74)' at baseline vs 12 at follow-up); only 5 of the 8 pre adjectives recur in the post set with a different index, so no item text was carried across. Live responses are RAW, not reverse-scored -- DECISIVE: reverse-scoring the four negative adjectives (upset, scared, hostile, irritable) and averaging all 8 reproduces the .sav's own precomputed composite column 'posaff_pre' EXACTLY, max absolute difference 0.0 over all 264 respondents, r = 1.000, mean 3.9001; the unreversed raw 8-item mean is 2.3139 and correlates only r = 0.331 with that composite. The paper states 'After reverse-scoring negative items, the PANAS showed acceptable reliability'. Rights: instrument_rights_register.csv carries PANAS (Watson, Clark & Tellegen 1988) verdict=ship -- APPLIED, not re-derived, and no register row written. Variant check per that row: this is an 8-adjective selection from the PANAS-20, not PANAS-X (60) or I-PANAS-SF (10). Gate: validate_items.R --table-sets PASS, item set 8/8 and resp set 1-5 exact; irw_table_sets() reports n=264 on all 8 items (2,112 rows), exactly matching the source file's 264 complete cases per column -- no row-count anomaly. Source .sav sha256 9e55bb22ae11dd41aede836743abf204a3f8cc3b565949c9975fdcef04f2f78a, independently re-fetched from PLOS on 2026-09-16 and byte-identical to the sibling rounds' cached copy.
public_note: Despite the table name and description, these 8 items are an 8-adjective selection from the PANAS and include four negative-affect adjectives (upset, scared, hostile, irritable) as well as four positive ones (proud, enthusiastic, interested, alert); the stored responses are raw, so the negative items must be reverse-scored before a positive-affect score is computed.
